key_insight: A PatternBoost-style loop combining local search with transformer-guided generation can discover new extremal geometric constructions that improve known lower bounds.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how learning-guided search can accelerate the discovery of hard instances and integrality gaps, informing algorithm design, benchmarking, and worst-case analysis.
method: Alternate local search with transformer-based candidate generation (PatternBoost/Axplorer).
Adapt representations, neighborhood moves, and surrogate ranking models to geometric combinatorial instances.
Use exact verification to validate promising candidates and iterate on discovered constructions.
evidence_signal: In three geometry problems, the tailored system found non-trivial constructions, including a stabbing-unit-squares gap of 20/13 and, with expert seeding, an improved 14/9 bound.
watch_item: Purely automated search plateaued quickly, indicating that representation quality and initial diversity strongly affect results and may limit full automation.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
